title: Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition
description: Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition stands as the oldest international competition aimed at individuals aged 18 years and under managed by the Royal Commonwealth society to build writing skills, address global issues in a creative manner, and to empower young voices.

title: Volunteer as a Judge for The Queen’s Commonwealth Writing Competition
description: Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition is looking for volunteer judges to rate thousands of students' essays internationally. Its goal is to engage individuals as much as they can into the competition as a way to champion the voices of the young competitors.
requirements: - Be over 19 years old, - Have an interest in writing and/or literature/ the Commonwealth and/or international affairs, - Be available between May 2026 and June 2026 in order to read and judge approximately 100-150 entries up to 1000 words each, - have reliable access to an internet connection during this period as the judging process is electronic. We also encourage that judges have access to a computer or laptop rather than phone to ensure full access to the judging platform.

title: Young Leaders And Changemakers Summer Camp
description: A 5-day action-packed summary camp that provides interactive workshops, group projects and live learning journeys ranging from policy-making to problem-solving, and work alongside peers from across the globe. It takes place in Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, NUS, Singapore.
requirements:
Cost: SGD 3,625 (regular); SGD 2,900 (early-bird discount), Aged 16+, Post-secondary, high-school or tertiary-level students, Aspiring youth leaders and changemakers
interested in public policy, governance, or social
innovation.

title: QS ImpACT Skills Challenge 2026
description: A global competition where teams design digital games that address real world problems tied to the UN SDG challenges. You can participate even if you’re new to coding.
requirements: Participants aged 18-35, team sizes 2-5

title: World IP Day Youth Video Competition 2026
description: Organised by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), this competition invites young creators (18–35) to produce a 60–90 second video about how intellectual property (IP) supports innovation and creativity in sports
requirements: Participants aged 18-35, Participants can join individual or up to teams of 10

title: The Mott Million Dollar Challenge
description: A national 30-90 second pitch competition for K-12 students in the United States. Funded by the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation to celebrate its centennial, the challenge invites young innovators to share ideas that improve their schools, homes, or communities.
requirements:
- You must live in the United States (50 States and Washington D.C.).
- You can go to public school, private school, charter school, homeschool, online school, or attend an out-of-school program.
- The children or wards of employees of the Mott Foundation, the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship (NFTE), and other affiliates are not eligible to win this competition. 
- You can make a team of up to three (3) students.  All team members must be in the same grade-level group (K-4, 5-8, 9-12).

title: International Astronomy and Astrophysics Competition (IAAC) 2026
description: An online science competition lets students explore astronomy, astrophysics, and maths through multiple rounds of problem solving. Participants get certificates and awards based on performance, and it’s open to high school and college students worldwide.
requirements:
Junior: 10th Grade and below (and < 16 years of age)
Youth: 11th to 13th Grade (and < 19 years of age)
Senior: 1st Year College/University and higher (or ≥ 19 years of age)

title: Global Futures Challenge Competition (Immerse Education)
description: A creative competition for students aged 14–18 where you submit a brief response (written, visual, or video) about your vision for the future and how your skills and goals could contribute to it.
requirements:
Age: You must be between 14 and 18 years old.
Nationality: The competition is open to students from any country and all school types.
Participation Type: You can enter individually or as part of a team of up to 4 members.

title: Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest 2026
description: The Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest is a premier annual competition for students aged 11–18 worldwide, designed to leverage art and creativity for ocean conservation. It encourages young people to explore, through various media, the human-driven impacts on the ocean, promoting environmental advocacy and activism.
requirements: Age: Must be between 11-18, Entries may be submitted by an individual or group of unlimited size

title: American Protégé International Music Talent Competition 2026
description: The American Protégé International Music Talent Competition is a worldwide competition for musicians of all ages and nationalities, focusing on genres like piano, strings, voice, and winds. It is designed to boost careers by offering winners a performance opportunity at the Weill Recital Hall at Carnegie Hall.
requirements: Applicants must submit an online application, a biography (max 150 words), a portrait photo, and pay an application fee.

title: Open Letters: The New York Times Opinion-Writing Contest
description: The New York Times Open Letter Contest is an annual opinion-writing competition for students (typically aged 13-19) to write a 500-word persuasive letter of protest or appeal to a specific, influential person or group.
requirements:
• Your piece must be, in total, 500 words or fewer, not including the title.
• You must be a student ages 13 to 19 in middle school or high school to participate. 
• You may work alone or in groups, but students should submit only one entry each.

title: My List: A Different Kind of Review Contest
description: The New York Times "My List" Review Contest is a, curated, multimedia contest where students (ages 13–19) curate 3-5 works of art/culture based on a theme and explain why others should check them out.
requirements:
• You must be a student ages 13 to 19 in middle school or high school to participate. 
• Your piece must be, in total, 600 words or fewer, not including the title.
• Your collection should only cover works that fit into the following categories of creative expression that The New York Times reviews.

title: Audio Stories: The New York Times Podcast Contest
description: The New York Times Student Podcast Contest invites students aged 13–19 worldwide to submit original audio stories (maximum 5 minutes) on any topic.
requirements: You must be a student ages 13 to 19 in middle school or high school to participate, be sure to use non-copyrighted sound effects or music, with some exceptions, and your piece should be no longer than five minutes.

title: Voice and Choice: The New York Times Summer Reading Contest
description: A weekly contest running over the summer in which students respond to journalism from The New York Times through short written reflections or brief videos. Best for students who enjoy reading, current events, and ongoing low-stakes writing practice.
requirements: Any teenager 13 to 19 years old anywhere in the world is invited to join,

title: The New York Times Conversation Challenge For Weekly Current Events
description: This challenge invites students to react to the news via our daily writing prompts, and each week. They publish a selection of their comments in a roundup for the world to read.

title: BBC Young Writers' Award 2026
description: BBC Young Writers' Award with Cambridge University challenges young people in the UK aged between 14-18 years to submit stories of up to 1,000 words.
requirements: Aged 14-18 and living in the UK.

title: Chinese Government Scholarships
description: The 2026/2027 Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS/CSC), administered by the China Scholarship Council, is a fully funded program for international students (Bachelor's, Master's, PhD) covering tuition, accommodation, stipend (CNY 2,500–3,500/month), and medical insurance

title: Young Leaders Program 2026 in Canada
description: This is a prestigious, fully-funded one-year initiative by the Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada. It aims to deepen connections between Canada and the Indo-Pacific through virtual seminars, networking, and a one-week in-person learning tour in Canada.
requirements:
Hold citizenship or permanent residency in an Indo-Pacific country/jurisdiction.
Education: An undergraduate degree (minimum) in a relevant field (e.g., Political Science, Public Policy, International Relations, Law, Economics, Sociology, History, Geography, Asian Studies, etc.).
Current graduate students are also eligible.
Experience: At least 5 years of relevant experience in one of the following sectors:
Government
International or regional organizations
Think-tanks
Media outlets
Business
Academia
Strong understanding, experience, and interest in:
Politics
Economics
Society
Diplomacy
International Relations
Security
History
Environmental Issues
The program is especially interested in early- to mid-career professionals.

title: China University of Petroleum CSC Scholarship 2026
description: This is now open for international applicants who aspire to pursue Undergraduate, Master’s, or PhD programs in China. This fully funded scholarship provides opportunities for students to gain world-class education and advanced research experience at one of China’s top universities.
requirements:
Applicants who are under 25 years old and have completed high school.
Master’s candidates: those under 35 with a bachelor’s degree.
Doctoral candidates: Those under 40 with a master’s degree.
Language prerequisites:
Depending on the program level, Chinese-taught programs require HSK 4 or 5.
IELTS 6.5, TOEFL 80, or documentation of English-medium training are prerequisites for English-taught programs.
Only residents of the Belt and Road nations are eligible for the Silk Road Program.
The particular prerequisites of each program must be fulfilled at the time of application.

title: Beijing Normal University CSC Scholarship 2026 in China
description: This scholarship is an exceptional opportunity for international students aiming to pursue graduate studies in China. This fully funded scholarship is designed to support outstanding students by covering tuition fees, living expenses, travel costs, and comprehensive health insurance.
requirements:
Not be receiving any other scholarships established by the Chinese government or social organizations.
Meet the degree and age requirements:
Undergraduate programs: must be a high school graduate and under 25 years old at the time of application.
Master’s programs: must hold a bachelor’s degree and be under 35 years old.
Doctoral programs: must hold a master’s degree and be under 40 years old.

title: Wuhan University CSC Scholarships 2026
description: This is now open for international students who wish to pursue fully funded higher education in China. This prestigious scholarship allows students from all over the world to study at Wuhan University without tuition fees.
requirements:
Foreign citizenship, and in good health.
Applicants who apply for a Master’s degree should be under 35 years old and have a Bachelor’s degree.
Applicants who apply for a doctoral degree should be under 40 years old and have a Master’s degree.
Applicants of Chinese-medium programs should have at least HSK level four certificate (Chinese Proficiency Test)
Applicants of English-medium programs should provide a score report of English Language test, TOEFL requires 80, IELTS requires 5.5 (You can apply without IELTS/TOEFL if you can take English Proficiency Certificate from your last attending Institution).

title: Sichuan University Chinese Government Scholarship 2026
description: This is for international students who want to pursue higher education. This fully funded program, offered under the CGS Type B – Chinese University Program, covers tuition fees, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living allowance, and comprehensive medical insurance for selected candidates.
requirements:
Must be a citizen of a country other than the People’s Republic of China.
Age limits:
Master’s applicants: under 35 years old
PhD applicants: under 40 years old
Academic qualifications:
Master’s: Bachelor’s degree
PhD: Master’s degree
Health: 
Good physical and mental health (Foreigner Physical Examination Form required)
Language proficiency:
Chinese-taught programs: HSK Level 4 (Science, Engineering, Medicine, Agriculture) or HSK Level 5 (Liberal Arts, Management, Law, Arts)
English-taught programs: TOEFL iBT ≥80 or IELTS ≥6 (non-native English speakers)
Must meet SCU departmental and university admission requirements.

title: Youth of Excellence Scheme Scholarship 2026
description: The Youth of Excellence Scheme Scholarship 2026 is a prestigious initiative by the Chinese Government, designed to attract talented international students eager to pursue advanced studies in China.
requirements:
Be a citizen of a country other than the People’s Republic of China and be under the age of 45, in good health both mentally and physically.
Have a bachelor’s degree or higher, with at least three years of work experience. Applicants with professional training or work experience related to the proposed program will be given preference.
Fall into one of the following four categories:
A government official at the division chief level (or equivalent) or above
A senior manager of an institution or enterprise
An administrator of a university or scientific research institution
An individual with relevant employment or internship experience in international organizations.
Ensure that the pre-admission letter provided by the university includes all necessary registration details—such as personal information, admission date, and major information—and does not contain any mention of having received or being promised a Chinese Government Scholarship.

title: OIST Research Internship 2026
description: The OIST Research Internship 2026 is a prestigious, fully funded 3–6 month program in Japan at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology, designed for STEM undergraduate/master's students and recent graduates.
requirements:
Those who are currently enrolled in their last two years of a bachelor's degree, enrolled in any year of a master's degree in universities, colleges, junior colleges, and vocational schools in Japan or overseas, or those who have graduated with a bachelor's or master's degree, are eligible to apply for the Research Internship at OIST.

Currently enrolled students must have approval from their home institution. The academic background of applicants should be appropriate to their desired host unit(s) at OIST.

Our Research Internship is intended for those who need more research experience and who are interested in joining OIST's PhD Program later. Current or graduated PhD students who wish to collaborate with OIST should look for other opportunities such as Workshops or Careers at OIST.

Research Interns who belong to a Japanese university/institution are required to prepare and bring their own insurances when accepted to the OIST Research Internship Program. Acceptable insurances are the combination of Gakkensai and Gakkenbai, or other insurances with similar coverage.

title: UNICEF Internship Programme
description: The UNICEF Internship Programme offers undergraduate, graduate, and recent graduates (within two years) hands-on, paid, 6–26 week opportunities to work in UNICEF offices globally
requirements:
• At least 18 years old.
• Enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or PhD programme, or have graduated within the past two years.
• Proficient in at least one of UNICEF's working languages: English, French or Spanish. Fluency in the working language of the office you are applying to, may also be required.
• Have no immediate relatives (e.g., mother, father, sister, brother) working with UNICEF, or any other relatives in your reporting line of authority.
• Have strong academic performance and motivation
• Additional consideration will be given to any professional experience relevant to the function you’re applying for.

title: Google Student Researcher, 2026 Program
description: The Google Student Researcher, 2026 program is a paid,, flexible, research-focused opportunity for Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD students to collaborate with teams like Google DeepMind and Google Research
requirements:
Minimum qualifications:
Currently enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree program in Computer Science, Linguistics, Statistics, Biostatistics, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Economics, or Natural Sciences.
Experience in one area of computer science (e.g., Natural Language Understanding, Human Computer Interactions, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Algorithmic Foundations of Optimization, Quantum Information Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, or similar areas).

Preferred qualifications:
Currently enrolled in a full-time degree program and returning to the program after completion of the internship.
Experience contributing research communities or efforts, including publishing papers in major conferences or journals.
Experience with one or more general purpose programming languages (e.g., Python, Java, JavaScript, C/C++, etc.).

title: Digital Business Apprenticeship (October 2026 Start)
description: The Digital Business Apprenticeship (October 2026 Start) at Google is a 15-to-24-month paid program in London (UK) designed for early-career professionals. It combines on-the-job training in Sales, Marketing, or Partnerships with academic study
requirements:
Minimum qualifications:
A pass at Level 2 for Maths and English.
Ability to communicate in English fluently to communicate with colleagues.

Preferred qualifications:
Ability to work independently and within a team framework.
Willingness to navigate ambiguous tasks, find suitable solutions and seek help/advice where appropriate.
Analytical mindset and comfortable with working with data to deliver insights and support outstanding creative execution
Enthusiasm and passion for measurement and new technologies, demonstrated through personal projects and interest in learning new skills.
Effective communication and organizational skills, proactive, self-motivated, positive attitude, and excellent customer service capabilities.
Strong project management skills.

title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory Summer Research Program
description: The MIT Lincoln Laboratory Summer Research Program is a competitive, paid, 10-12 week internship (mid-May to mid-August) for undergraduate and graduate students, offering hands-on R&D in national security, engineering, and science, typically at their Lexington, MA site.
requirements: To be eligible for the Summer Research Program, students must have at least completed their sophomore year of college or be enrolled in a master's or doctoral program.  In addition, students must have maintained an excellent academic record and be a U.S. citizen.

title: OECD Internship Programme
description: The OECD Internship Programme offers motivated students from diverse backgrounds a chance to support evidence-based policy work at the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
requirements:
Are enrolled in a full-time degree programme* for the duration of the internship in a field or discipline related to the work of the OECD
Are available for a minimum internship duration of one month
Have an excellent command of one of the two official languages of the OECD (English and French) and a working knowledge of, or willingness to learn, the other. Knowledge of other languages could be an advantage
Have good quantitative and IT skills
Have good drafting and communication skills
Thrive in a multicultural and international team environment.

title: International Economics Olympiad
description: The International Economics Olympiad (IEO) is an annual global competition for high school students designed to foster creative problem-solving in economics, business, and finance. Founded in 2018, it aims to identify and encourage young talent in these fields.
deadline: Deadline For Official Team Applications: 30 April, 2026
requirements:
Age Limit: Contestants must have been born after June 30, 2006 (meaning they must be under 20 years old on June 30, 2026).
Educational Status: As of December 1, 2025, students must have been working toward receiving a high school (secondary school) diploma or an equivalent degree.
Academic Level: The competition is designed for students at ISCED Level 3 (typically senior high school). Students who have already started tertiary-level (university) studies are ineligible.
Residency/Citizenship: Contestants must be citizens or residents of the country they represent. International students attending school in a participating country on a student visa or residency permit are also eligible to join that country's team.

title: International Young Physicists' Tournament
description: This is a prestigious annual team-based scientific competition for secondary school students. Teams research 17 open-ended, complex physics problems over several months, presenting and defending their solutions against opponents in structured "Physics Fights" evaluated by international experts.
requirements:
Student Status: Participants must be secondary school students or have graduated in the same calendar year as the tournament.
Team Size: Teams consist of 3 to 5 students.
Citizenship/Residence: Members must be citizens of the country they represent or be enrolled in a school in that country.
Team Leader: Each team must have a team leader (often a teacher or mentor).
Application Process: Teams usually qualify through national tournaments (e.g., CaYPT in Canada, USAYPT in the USA).
Language: The competition is held in English.
Experience: Teams generally cannot change their composition during the tournament.

title: International Greenwich Olympiad
description: This is a prestigious global project-based competition for students aged 10–19, hosted by North London Grammar School in London. It challenges young minds to innovate solutions for global issues, particularly in sustainability, engineering, and science, aligned with UN SDGs.
requirements: Secondary school students who are aged between 13 and 18 years old. Students are welcome to participate as individuals or in team of maximum three, not necessarily from the same school.

title: World Maths Day 2026
description: This is a global, 24-hour online competition occurring on March 25, 2026, where students aged 4-18 compete in live, 60-second math games. It challenges learners to solve mental arithmetic problems against others worldwide. The 2026 theme is "United by Numbers".
requirements: Open to students aged 5 to 18.

title: World Scholar's Cup
description: The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is a premier international academic program and competition for students, bringing together over 50,000 participants from 60+ countries annually.
deadline: Deadlines are approaching quickly, with some, such as the one mentioned for early 2026, closing on March 1, 2026.
requirements:
Divisions:
Skittles (Junior): Ages 8–12.
Junior Division: Typically ages 11–13 (born on or after Jan 1, 2012, for 2026).
Senior Division: Ages 14+ (born before Jan 1, 2012, for 2026).
Academic Level: Students up to their final year of pre-university schooling (high school, A-levels, IB).
Team Structure: Teams of 3 (preferred) or 2 members.
Independent Participants: Students can register independently or as part of a school team.
Language: Competitions are conducted in English.

title: Science Without Borders Art Challenge
description: The Science Without Borders® Challenge is an annual international art contest run by the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation that engages students aged 11–19 in marine science and ocean conservation.
requirements:
All students ages 11-19 who are enrolled in primary or secondary school, or the home school equivalent anywhere in the world may enter the Science Without Borders® Challenge. Students age 10 may participate as long as they turn 11 by March 2, 2026. College and university students are not eligible for this contest. Proof of age, identity, and/or eligibility may be required.
All artwork must be an original work by the contestant and shall not infringe on any copyrights or any other rights of any third parties. Do not copy an idea from a past participants’ work. Do not draw a character from a cartoon or movie. See the tips for success and grading rubric for more information on what the judges are (and are not) looking for.
Do not submit artwork to the Science Without Borders® Challenge that you have entered into another art competition or a previous Science Without Borders® Challenge.

title: Nami Island International Picture Book Illustration Concours
description: The Nami Island International Picture Book Illustration Concours (Nami Concours) is a major biennial international competition held in South Korea since 2013, aimed at encouraging creativity and enhancing the quality of children's book illustrations.

title: Earth Partner Prize
description: The Earth Partner Prize (formerly #CreateCOP) is an annual international art competition for creatives aged 14–30, designed to accelerate climate action through culture
requirements: Artists, creatives, and photographers aged 14–30.

title: International Thespian Festival
description: The International Thespian Festival (ITF) is a premier annual, week-long event for student members of the Educational Theatre Association (EdTA), celebrating middle and high school theater through performances, workshops, and college auditions.
deadline: Deadline: Standard Registration: 4 February, 2026-30 April, 2026 and Late Registration: 1 May, 2026-13 May, 2026
requirements:
Participants: Students in grades 6-12.
Adult Leaders/Chaperones: Must be at least 21 years old.
Chaperone Requirement: All students must be chaperoned for the entire week, with gender-specific supervision (female students with a female chaperone, male students with a male chaperone) recommended.
Registration Process: Opens in early February (e.g., Feb 4, 2026), with options for individual or troupe registration.
Safety: Background checks are required for all attendees aged 18+.
College Auditions (Optional): Limited to inducted Thespians graduating in 2027 (rising seniors).
Non-Affiliated Students: Students not in an active troupe may attend but must still be accompanied by an registered adult chaperone.

title: Golden Classical Music Awards
description: The Golden Classical Music Awards (GCMA) is an international competition designed to discover young musicians across strings, piano, wind, and vocal disciplines and launch their careers with opportunities like a performance at Carnegie Hall's Weill Recital Hall in New York.
requirements:
Disciplines: Piano, Strings (Violin, Viola, Cello, Double Bass, Guitar), Woodwinds (Flute, Oboe, Clarinet, Bassoon, Saxophone, Recorder), Brass (French Horn, Trumpet, Trombone, Tuba), and Vocal (Female/Male).
Ensembles: Piano duo, piano four-hands, and mixed chamber ensembles.
Age Categories: Open to all ages, generally divided into groups such as Young Musician (under 12), Junior (13-18), and Senior (18+).
Repertoire: One, two, or three pieces from Baroque, Classical, Romantic, or Contemporary periods.
Submission Material: Video or audio recordings must be submitted; they should represent the contestant's abilities but do not need professional-quality production.
Application: A completed online application form and payment of the non-refundable fee are required.

title: All American High School Film Festival
description: It's the world's largest, premier film festival for high school students. It provides a major platform for young filmmakers to screen their work, network with industry professionals, attend workshops, and win over $3.5 million in scholarships and prizes.
deadline: Free Submission Deadline: 2 March, 2026, Regular Submission Deadline: 27 April, 2026, Late Submission Deadline: 25 May, 2026, Final Deadline: 3 July, 2026
requirements:
Target Demographic: Current high school students or those who graduated in the same year as the festival.
Originality: Films must be created by the student(s).
Technical Specs: Minimum 1080p resolution, submitted in .mp4 or .mov format.
Content Restrictions: No copyrighted music/images (must use licensed or original).
Runtime: Varies by category, generally up to 40 minutes for shorts, 90 minutes for features.
Submission Platform: Typically through FilmFreeway.
Deadlines: Early bird (typically March), Regular (July), and Late (August).
Awards: Attendance is not required to win, but encouraged.

title: International Biology Olympiad (IBO)
description: It's the premier annual worldwide biology competition for top-performing pre-university students. It challenges gifted students through rigorous theoretical and practical exams, fostering talent in life sciences, promoting scientific careers, and facilitating international networking among young biologists from over 75 countries.
requirements:
National Selection: You must win your country's official National Biology Olympiad (NBO). The IBO does not allow independent, direct registration.
Age Limit: Candidates must be under 20 years old as of July 1 of the competition year.
Education Level: You must be a student in a regular secondary school (general education) and not have started full-time university/college studies.
Participation Limit: A student may participate in the IBO a maximum of two times.
Citizenship/Residence: You must represent your country of citizenship or long-term residence.
Training Restriction: Participants cannot have received specific IBO training in a group of 50 or fewer students for more than two weeks.

title: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
description: The International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO) is a premier annual academic competition for secondary school students, bringing together the world's most talented young minds in chemistry.
requirements:
Age: Under 20 years old on July 1 of the competition year.
Education: Secondary school students or recent graduates not yet in university.
Selection: Must be chosen through their country’s National Chemistry Olympiad.
Nationality: Participants must be citizens or passport holders of the country they represent.
Team Size: Each country sends a team of up to 4 students.
Previous Winners: Gold medal winners from previous IChO competitions are generally not eligible to compete again.

title: MUN Paris 2026
description: A major MUN conference held in Paris, France, from March 24–26, 2026, as part of the MUN EUROPE network---inviting high schools and universities to debate global issues, develop diplomatic skills, and simulate UN procedures in English or French.
requirements:
Target Audience: Students from high schools and colleges/universities.
Experience Level: Open to both beginners and experienced delegates.
Requirements:
Submission of a position paper (deadline typically around Oct 2025 for a spring 2026 event).
Visa for travel (if applicable).
Language: The simulation is conducted in English.
Location: Paris, France (venue often at hotels like Hôtel Mercure Paris Centre Tour Eiffel).

title: WIMUN Singapore 2026
description: WIMUN Singapore 2026 is the Southeast Asian edition of the WFUNA International Model United Nations (WIMUN) conference, widely recognized as the world's most accurate simulation of the United Nations
deadline:
Early Registration: February 28, 2026
Priority Registration: May 31, 2026
Regular Registration: June 30, 2026
requirements:
Target Audience: Students (High School, University, Grad School) and young professionals aged 14–30.
Experience Level: Open to beginners and experienced MUN participants, though familiarity with the WIMUN Approach is helpful.
Geography: Open to participants from North America, Europe, Asia, South America, Africa, and Oceania.
Requirements: High school students must have a chaperone. Individuals or groups can register.
Registration Deadline: Early bird deadline is Feb 28, 2026, and priority deadline is May 31, 2026.
Venue: Suntec Convention Centre, Singapore.
Cost: Delegate fees are $289, with no scholarships offered by WFUNA.

title: John Peters Humphrey MUN 2026
description: It's a 3-day, in-person educational conference for high school students, held at St. Thomas University in Fredericton, NB from May 1–3, 2026. It simulates UN proceedings to teach diplomacy, research, and public speaking.
deadline:
Early Bird Deadline: February 24, 2026.
Final Registration Deadline: March 24, 2026
requirements: Generally open to high school and university students interested in debating international affairs.

title: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair
description: The Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) is the world's largest pre-college STEM competition, held annually in the U.S. and managed by the Society for Science.
deadline:
Mid-February 2026: Registration opens for all approved affiliated fairs.
By February 9, 2026: Official Party Registration becomes available online.
Within 12 Days of Fair: Finalist Questionnaire and Official Party Registration must be submitted after your local/regional fair.
April 13, 2026: Last day to hold an affiliated fair.
April 30, 2026: Deadline for registration fee checks/transfers to be postmarked.
requirements:
Grade Level: Students must be in grades 9–12 or equivalent.
Age: Students must not have reached age 20 on or before May 1st of the competition year.
Qualification: Students must compete in and win the right to attend from a Society for Science-affiliated fair.
Project Scope: Projects can be individual or team-based (maximum 3 members).
Research Duration: Projects can include a maximum of 12 months of continuous research, and must not include research performed more than 18 months before the competition.
Categories: The project must fit into one of the 22 ISEF categories.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
description: The Breakthrough Junior Challenge is a global, annual science video competition for students aged 13–18 to explain complex concepts in life sciences, physics, or math via a < 2-minute video
requirements:
Age: Must be at least 13 years old by May 1, 2025, and not older than 18 (not yet 19) on October 1, 2025.
Location: Open globally, provided the applicant does not reside in a country subject to U.S. sanctions.
Language: Submissions must be in English.

title: Adobe Certified Professional World Championship
description: Certiport's Adobe Certified Professional World Championship, formerly known as Adobe Certified Associate (ACA) World Championship, is a global competition that tests students' design skills using Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign
requirements:
Student Status: Must be enrolled in an accredited academic institution.
Age: 13 to 22 years old as of December 31, 2026.
Certification: Must earn an Adobe Certified Professional certification in Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, or InDesign.
Project Submission: Must submit an original design project for the qualifying rounds.
Restrictions: Employees of Adobe, Certiport, and their affiliates are ineligible.
Prior Winners: Previous top 3 winners of the World Championship are generally not eligible.

title: Tel-Aviv International Student Film Festival
description: It's the world's largest and most prestigious student film festival, founded in 1986 by Tel Aviv University students. Held annually in June at the Tel Aviv Cinematheque, it showcases over 150 short films from 50+ countries.
requirements:
Applicant Status: Films must be made within school programs, universities, or professional institutes.
Production Date: Completed during 2025-2026.
Length: Up to 30 minutes.
Submission Limit: Each school may submit up to 3 films.
Subtitles: English subtitles are required for all films, including English-speaking ones.
Premiere Status: No premiere status required.

Applicants who apply for a doctoral degree should be under 40 years old and have a Master’s degree.
Applicants of Chinese-medium programs should have at least HSK level four certificate (Chinese Proficiency Test)
Applicants of English-medium programs should provide a score report of English Language test, TOEFL requires 80, IELTS requires 5.5 (You can apply without IELTS/TOEFL if you can take English Proficiency Certificate from your last attending Institution).

title: Sichuan University Chinese Government Scholarship 2026
description: This is for international students who want to pursue higher education. This fully funded program, offered under the CGS Type B – Chinese University Program, covers tuition fees, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living allowance, and comprehensive medical insurance for selected candidates.
requirements:
Must be a citizen of a country other than the People’s Republic of China.
Age limits:
Master’s applicants: under 35 years old
PhD applicants: under 40 years old
Academic qualifications:
Master’s: Bachelor’s degree
PhD: Master’s degree
Health: 
Good physical and mental health (Foreigner Physical Examination Form required)
Language proficiency:
Chinese-taught programs: HSK Level 4 (Science, Engineering, Medicine, Agriculture) or HSK Level 5 (Liberal Arts, Management, Law, Arts)
English-taught programs: TOEFL iBT ≥80 or IELTS ≥6 (non-native English speakers)
Must meet SCU departmental and university admission requirements.

title: Youth of Excellence Scheme Scholarship 2026
description: The Youth of Excellence Scheme Scholarship 2026 is a prestigious initiative by the Chinese Government, designed to attract talented international students eager to pursue advanced studies in China.
requirements:
Be a citizen of a country other than the People’s Republic of China and be under the age of 45, in good health both mentally and physically.
Have a bachelor’s degree or higher, with at least three years of work experience. Applicants with professional training or work experience related to the proposed program will be given preference.
Fall into one of the following four categories:
A government official at the division chief level (or equivalent) or above
A senior manager of an institution or enterprise
An administrator of a university or scientific research institution
An individual with relevant employment or internship experience in international organizations.
Ensure that the pre-admission letter provided by the university includes all necessary registration details—such as personal information, admission date, and major information—and does not contain any mention of having received or being promised a Chinese Government Scholarship.

title: OIST Research Internship 2026
description: The OIST Research Internship 2026 is a prestigious, fully funded 3–6 month program in Japan at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology, designed for STEM undergraduate/master's students and recent graduates.
requirements:
Those who are currently enrolled in their last two years of a bachelor's degree, enrolled in any year of a master's degree in universities, colleges, junior colleges, and vocational schools in Japan or overseas, or those who have graduated with a bachelor's or master's degree, are eligible to apply for the Research Internship at OIST.

Currently enrolled students must have approval from their home institution. The academic background of applicants should be appropriate to their desired host unit(s) at OIST.

Our Research Internship is intended for those who need more research experience and who are interested in joining OIST's PhD Program later. Current or graduated PhD students who wish to collaborate with OIST should look for other opportunities such as Workshops or Careers at OIST.

Research Interns who belong to a Japanese university/institution are required to prepare and bring their own insurances when accepted to the OIST Research Internship Program. Acceptable insurances are the combination of Gakkensai and Gakkenbai, or other insurances with similar coverage.

title: UNICEF Internship Programme
description: The UNICEF Internship Programme offers undergraduate, graduate, and recent graduates (within two years) hands-on, paid, 6–26 week opportunities to work in UNICEF offices globally
requirements:
• At least 18 years old.
• Enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or PhD programme, or have graduated within the past two years.
• Proficient in at least one of UNICEF's working languages: English, French or Spanish. Fluency in the working language of the office you are applying to, may also be required.
• Have no immediate relatives (e.g., mother, father, sister, brother) working with UNICEF, or any other relatives in your reporting line of authority.
• Have strong academic performance and motivation
• Additional consideration will be given to any professional experience relevant to the function you’re applying for.

title: Google Student Researcher, 2026 Program
description: The Google Student Researcher, 2026 program is a paid,, flexible, research-focused opportunity for Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD students to collaborate with teams like Google DeepMind and Google Research
requirements:
Minimum qualifications:
Currently enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree program in Computer Science, Linguistics, Statistics, Biostatistics, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Economics, or Natural Sciences.
Experience in one area of computer science (e.g., Natural Language Understanding, Human Computer Interactions, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Algorithmic Foundations of Optimization, Quantum Information Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, or similar areas).

Preferred qualifications:
Currently enrolled in a full-time degree program and returning to the program after completion of the internship.
Experience contributing research communities or efforts, including publishing papers in major conferences or journals.
Experience with one or more general purpose programming languages (e.g., Python, Java, JavaScript, C/C++, etc.).

title: Digital Business Apprenticeship (October 2026 Start)
description: The Digital Business Apprenticeship (October 2026 Start) at Google is a 15-to-24-month paid program in London (UK) designed for early-career professionals. It combines on-the-job training in Sales, Marketing, or Partnerships with academic study
requirements:
Minimum qualifications:
A pass at Level 2 for Maths and English.
Ability to communicate in English fluently to communicate with colleagues.

Preferred qualifications:
Ability to work independently and within a team framework.
Willingness to navigate ambiguous tasks, find suitable solutions and seek help/advice where appropriate.
Analytical mindset and comfortable with working with data to deliver insights and support outstanding creative execution
Enthusiasm and passion for measurement and new technologies, demonstrated through personal projects and interest in learning new skills.
Effective communication and organizational skills, proactive, self-motivated, positive attitude, and excellent customer service capabilities.
Strong project management skills.

title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory Summer Research Program
description: The MIT Lincoln Laboratory Summer Research Program is a competitive, paid, 10-12 week internship (mid-May to mid-August) for undergraduate and graduate students, offering hands-on R&D in national security, engineering, and science, typically at their Lexington, MA site.
requirements: To be eligible for the Summer Research Program, students must have at least completed their sophomore year of college or be enrolled in a master's or doctoral program.  In addition, students must have maintained an excellent academic record and be a U.S. citizen.

title: OECD Internship Programme
description: The OECD Internship Programme offers motivated students from diverse backgrounds a chance to support evidence-based policy work at the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
requirements:
Are enrolled in a full-time degree programme* for the duration of the internship in a field or discipline related to the work of the OECD
Are available for a minimum internship duration of one month
Have an excellent command of one of the two official languages of the OECD (English and French) and a working knowledge of, or willingness to learn, the other. Knowledge of other languages could be an advantage
Have good quantitative and IT skills
Have good drafting and communication skills
Thrive in a multicultural and international team environment.

title: International Economics Olympiad
description: The International Economics Olympiad (IEO) is an annual global competition for high school students designed to foster creative problem-solving in economics, business, and finance. Founded in 2018, it aims to identify and encourage young talent in these fields.
deadline: Deadline For Official Team Applications: 30 April, 2026
requirements:
Age Limit: Contestants must have been born after June 30, 2006 (meaning they must be under 20 years old on June 30, 2026).
Educational Status: As of December 1, 2025, students must have been working toward receiving a high school (secondary school) diploma or an equivalent degree.
Academic Level: The competition is designed for students at ISCED Level 3 (typically senior high school). Students who have already started tertiary-level (university) studies are ineligible.
Residency/Citizenship: Contestants must be citizens or residents of the country they represent. International students attending school in a participating country on a student visa or residency permit are also eligible to join that country's team.

title: International Young Physicists' Tournament
description: This is a prestigious annual team-based scientific competition for secondary school students. Teams research 17 open-ended, complex physics problems over several months, presenting and defending their solutions against opponents in structured "Physics Fights" evaluated by international experts.
requirements:
Student Status: Participants must be secondary school students or have graduated in the same calendar year as the tournament.
Team Size: Teams consist of 3 to 5 students.
Citizenship/Residence: Members must be citizens of the country they represent or be enrolled in a school in that country.
Team Leader: Each team must have a team leader (often a teacher or mentor).
Application Process: Teams usually qualify through national tournaments (e.g., CaYPT in Canada, USAYPT in the USA).
Language: The competition is held in English.
Experience: Teams generally cannot change their composition during the tournament.

title: International Greenwich Olympiad
description: This is a prestigious global project-based competition for students aged 10–19, hosted by North London Grammar School in London. It challenges young minds to innovate solutions for global issues, particularly in sustainability, engineering, and science, aligned with UN SDGs.
requirements: Secondary school students who are aged between 13 and 18 years old. Students are welcome to participate as individuals or in team of maximum three, not necessarily from the same school.

title: World Maths Day 2026
description: This is a global, 24-hour online competition occurring on March 25, 2026, where students aged 4-18 compete in live, 60-second math games. It challenges learners to solve mental arithmetic problems against others worldwide. The 2026 theme is "United by Numbers".
requirements: Open to students aged 5 to 18.

title: World Scholar's Cup
description: The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is a premier international academic program and competition for students, bringing together over 50,000 participants from 60+ countries annually.
deadline: Deadlines are approaching quickly, with some, such as the one mentioned for early 2026, closing on March 1, 2026.
requirements:
Divisions:
Skittles (Junior): Ages 8–12.
Junior Division: Typically ages 11–13 (born on or after Jan 1, 2012, for 2026).
Senior Division: Ages 14+ (born before Jan 1, 2012, for 2026).
Academic Level: Students up to their final year of pre-university schooling (high school, A-levels, IB).
Team Structure: Teams of 3 (preferred) or 2 members.
Independent Participants: Students can register independently or as part of a school team.
Language: Competitions are conducted in English.

title: Science Without Borders Art Challenge
description: The Science Without Borders® Challenge is an annual international art contest run by the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation that engages students aged 11–19 in marine science and ocean conservation.
requirements:
All students ages 11-19 who are enrolled in primary or secondary school, or the home school equivalent anywhere in the world may enter the Science Without Borders® Challenge. Students age 10 may participate as long as they turn 11 by March 2, 2026. College and university students are not eligible for this contest. Proof of age, identity, and/or eligibility may be required.
All artwork must be an original work by the contestant and shall not infringe on any copyrights or any other rights of any third parties. Do not copy an idea from a past participants’ work. Do not draw a character from a cartoon or movie. See the tips for success and grading rubric for more information on what the judges are (and are not) looking for.
Do not submit artwork to the Science Without Borders® Challenge that you have entered into another art competition or a previous Science Without Borders® Challenge.

title: Nami Island International Picture Book Illustration Concours
description: The Nami Island International Picture Book Illustration Concours (Nami Concours) is a major biennial international competition held in South Korea since 2013, aimed at encouraging creativity and enhancing the quality of children's book illustrations.

title: Earth Partner Prize
description: The Earth Partner Prize (formerly #CreateCOP) is an annual international art competition for creatives aged 14–30, designed to accelerate climate action through culture
requirements: Artists, creatives, and photographers aged 14–30.

title: International Thespian Festival
description: The International Thespian Festival (ITF) is a premier annual, week-long event for student members of the Educational Theatre Association (EdTA), celebrating middle and high school theater through performances, workshops, and college auditions.
deadline: Deadline: Standard Registration: 4 February, 2026-30 April, 2026 and Late Registration: 1 May, 2026-13 May, 2026
requirements:
Participants: Students in grades 6-12.
Adult Leaders/Chaperones: Must be at least 21 years old.
Chaperone Requirement: All students must be chaperoned for the entire week, with gender-specific supervision (female students with a female chaperone, male students with a male chaperone) recommended.
Registration Process: Opens in early February (e.g., Feb 4, 2026), with options for individual or troupe registration.
Safety: Background checks are required for all attendees aged 18+.
College Auditions (Optional): Limited to inducted Thespians graduating in 2027 (rising seniors).
Non-Affiliated Students: Students not in an active troupe may attend but must still be accompanied by an registered adult chaperone.

title: Golden Classical Music Awards
description: The Golden Classical Music Awards (GCMA) is an international competition designed to discover young musicians across strings, piano, wind, and vocal disciplines and launch their careers with opportunities like a performance at Carnegie Hall's Weill Recital Hall in New York.
requirements:
Disciplines: Piano, Strings (Violin, Viola, Cello, Double Bass, Guitar), Woodwinds (Flute, Oboe, Clarinet, Bassoon, Saxophone, Recorder), Brass (French Horn, Trumpet, Trombone, Tuba), and Vocal (Female/Male).
Ensembles: Piano duo, piano four-hands, and mixed chamber ensembles.
Age Categories: Open to all ages, generally divided into groups such as Young Musician (under 12), Junior (13-18), and Senior (18+).
Repertoire: One, two, or three pieces from Baroque, Classical, Romantic, or Contemporary periods.
Submission Material: Video or audio recordings must be submitted; they should represent the contestant's abilities but do not need professional-quality production.
Application: A completed online application form and payment of the non-refundable fee are required.

title: All American High School Film Festival
description: It's the world's largest, premier film festival for high school students. It provides a major platform for young filmmakers to screen their work, network with industry professionals, attend workshops, and win over $3.5 million in scholarships and prizes.
deadline: Free Submission Deadline: 2 March, 2026, Regular Submission Deadline: 27 April, 2026, Late Submission Deadline: 25 May, 2026, Final Deadline: 3 July, 2026
requirements:
Target Demographic: Current high school students or those who graduated in the same year as the festival.
Originality: Films must be created by the student(s).
Technical Specs: Minimum 1080p resolution, submitted in .mp4 or .mov format.
Content Restrictions: No copyrighted music/images (must use licensed or original).
Runtime: Varies by category, generally up to 40 minutes for shorts, 90 minutes for features.
Submission Platform: Typically through FilmFreeway.
Deadlines: Early bird (typically March), Regular (July), and Late (August).
Awards: Attendance is not required to win, but encouraged.

title: International Biology Olympiad (IBO)
description: It's the premier annual worldwide biology competition for top-performing pre-university students. It challenges gifted students through rigorous theoretical and practical exams, fostering talent in life sciences, promoting scientific careers, and facilitating international networking among young biologists from over 75 countries.
requirements:
National Selection: You must win your country's official National Biology Olympiad (NBO). The IBO does not allow independent, direct registration.
Age Limit: Candidates must be under 20 years old as of July 1 of the competition year.
Education Level: You must be a student in a regular secondary school (general education) and not have started full-time university/college studies.
Participation Limit: A student may participate in the IBO a maximum of two times.
Citizenship/Residence: You must represent your country of citizenship or long-term residence.
Training Restriction: Participants cannot have received specific IBO training in a group of 50 or fewer students for more than two weeks.

title: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
description: The International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO) is a premier annual academic competition for secondary school students, bringing together the world's most talented young minds in chemistry.
requirements:
Age: Under 20 years old on July 1 of the competition year.
Education: Secondary school students or recent graduates not yet in university.
Selection: Must be chosen through their country’s National Chemistry Olympiad.
Nationality: Participants must be citizens or passport holders of the country they represent.
Team Size: Each country sends a team of up to 4 students.
Previous Winners: Gold medal winners from previous IChO competitions are generally not eligible to compete again.

title: MUN Paris 2026
description: A major MUN conference held in Paris, France, from March 24–26, 2026, as part of the MUN EUROPE network---inviting high schools and universities to debate global issues, develop diplomatic skills, and simulate UN procedures in English or French.
requirements:
Target Audience: Students from high schools and colleges/universities.
Experience Level: Open to both beginners and experienced delegates.
Requirements:
Submission of a position paper (deadline typically around Oct 2025 for a spring 2026 event).
Visa for travel (if applicable).
Language: The simulation is conducted in English.
Location: Paris, France (venue often at hotels like Hôtel Mercure Paris Centre Tour Eiffel).

title: WIMUN Singapore 2026
description: WIMUN Singapore 2026 is the Southeast Asian edition of the WFUNA International Model United Nations (WIMUN) conference, widely recognized as the world's most accurate simulation of the United Nations
deadline:
Early Registration: February 28, 2026
Priority Registration: May 31, 2026
Regular Registration: June 30, 2026
requirements:
Target Audience: Students (High School, University, Grad School) and young professionals aged 14–30.
Experience Level: Open to beginners and experienced MUN participants, though familiarity with the WIMUN Approach is helpful.
Geography: Open to participants from North America, Europe, Asia, South America, Africa, and Oceania.
Requirements: High school students must have a chaperone. Individuals or groups can register.
Registration Deadline: Early bird deadline is Feb 28, 2026, and priority deadline is May 31, 2026.
Venue: Suntec Convention Centre, Singapore.
Cost: Delegate fees are $289, with no scholarships offered by WFUNA.

title: John Peters Humphrey MUN 2026
description: It's a 3-day, in-person educational conference for high school students, held at St. Thomas University in Fredericton, NB from May 1–3, 2026. It simulates UN proceedings to teach diplomacy, research, and public speaking.
deadline:
Early Bird Deadline: February 24, 2026.
Final Registration Deadline: March 24, 2026
requirements: Generally open to high school and university students interested in debating international affairs.

title: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair
description: The Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) is the world's largest pre-college STEM competition, held annually in the U.S. and managed by the Society for Science.
deadline:
Mid-February 2026: Registration opens for all approved affiliated fairs.
By February 9, 2026: Official Party Registration becomes available online.
Within 12 Days of Fair: Finalist Questionnaire and Official Party Registration must be submitted after your local/regional fair.
April 13, 2026: Last day to hold an affiliated fair.
April 30, 2026: Deadline for registration fee checks/transfers to be postmarked.
requirements:
Grade Level: Students must be in grades 9–12 or equivalent.
Age: Students must not have reached age 20 on or before May 1st of the competition year.
Qualification: Students must compete in and win the right to attend from a Society for Science-affiliated fair.
Project Scope: Projects can be individual or team-based (maximum 3 members).
Research Duration: Projects can include a maximum of 12 months of continuous research, and must not include research performed more than 18 months before the competition.
Categories: The project must fit into one of the 22 ISEF categories.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
description: The Breakthrough Junior Challenge is a global, annual science video competition for students aged 13–18 to explain complex concepts in life sciences, physics, or math via a < 2-minute video
requirements:
Age: Must be at least 13 years old by May 1, 2025, and not older than 18 (not yet 19) on October 1, 2025.
Location: Open globally, provided the applicant does not reside in a country subject to U.S. sanctions.
Language: Submissions must be in English.

title: Adobe Certified Professional World Championship
description: Certiport's Adobe Certified Professional World Championship, formerly known as Adobe Certified Associate (ACA) World Championship, is a global competition that tests students' design skills using Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign
requirements:
Student Status: Must be enrolled in an accredited academic institution.
Age: 13 to 22 years old as of December 31, 2026.
Certification: Must earn an Adobe Certified Professional certification in Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, or InDesign.
Project Submission: Must submit an original design project for the qualifying rounds.
Restrictions: Employees of Adobe, Certiport, and their affiliates are ineligible.
Prior Winners: Previous top 3 winners of the World Championship are generally not eligible.

title: Tel-Aviv International Student Film Festival
description: It's the world's largest and most prestigious student film festival, founded in 1986 by Tel Aviv University students. Held annually in June at the Tel Aviv Cinematheque, it showcases over 150 short films from 50+ countries.
requirements:
Applicant Status: Films must be made within school programs, universities, or professional institutes.
Production Date: Completed during 2025-2026.
Length: Up to 30 minutes.
Submission Limit: Each school may submit up to 3 films.
Subtitles: English subtitles are required for all films, including English-speaking ones.
Premiere Status: No premiere status required.
Format: Screeners must be enabled for download.
Experimental/Video Art: Students or graduates (within 5 years) can submit to this category.

title: ImagiNation Student Film Festival
description: The ImagiNation International Student Film Festival (INISFF) is a global platform designed to nurture, showcase, and celebrate the creativity, storytelling, and filmmaking skills of young filmmakers.
deadline:
Extended Deadline: March 23, 2026
Notification Date: April 10, 2026
requirements: Target Audience: Students and first-time filmmakers aged 11–18 (specifically mentioned in Instagram post), extending up to university (UG & PG) levels.

title: International Genetically Engineered Machine Competition (iGEM)
description: The International Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) Competition is the world's premier synthetic biology competition, where multidisciplinary student teams (undergraduate, high school, and graduate) design and build biological systems using standardized, open-source genetic parts
deadline:
Regular Registration Deadline: April 2, 2026 (15:00 UTC)
Late Registration Deadline: June 4, 2026 (15:00 UTC)
requirements:
Team Composition: Teams are generally formed within universities (Collegiate), high schools, or community labs.
Age Requirement: All team members must be at least 13 years old as of March 31, 2026.
Supervision: Each team must have a Primary PI who is a faculty member, teacher, or director of a community lab.
Project Focus: Projects must involve synthetic biology and adhere to safety guidelines.
Documentation: Teams must document their work on a team wiki and submit safety forms.
Community Labs: Teams from community labs must demonstrate access to a Biosafety Level 1 (BSL-1) lab, have a safety training program, and be an incorporated entity.
